objective.text: Store a hash of a reset token while verifying the presented plaintext token through the repository.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish the link token from its stored verification representation.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A DatabaseTokenRepository creates a reset token and returns it for the link. Is the token column expected to equal that returned string?

options.text: No; the stored token is hashed, and the repository checks the presented token against that hash.
options.rationale: The database stores a verification hash while the link carries the generated token.

options.text: Yes; hashing applies only after the first successful reset.
options.rationale: The hash is written when the token record is created.
options.misconception: The hash is written when the token record is created.

options.text: Yes; the repository compares link tokens with plaintext SQL equality.
options.rationale: The repository verifies with the configured hasher instead of storing the returned token unchanged.
options.misconception: The repository verifies with the configured hasher instead of storing the returned token unchanged.

options.text: No; the token column contains an encrypted email address instead.
options.rationale: The email identifies the record separately; the token column stores the token hash.
options.misconception: The email identifies the record separately; the token column stores the token hash.
